Function added to src/reports.js:
```javascript
export function vatSummary(invoices) {
  const vatMap = new Map();

  invoices
    .filter((inv) => inv.status === 'issued' || inv.status === 'partially_paid' || inv.status === 'paid')
    .forEach((inv) => {
      inv.lines.forEach((line) => {
        const rate = line.vatRate;
        const base = lineTotal(line) - lineDiscount(line);
        const vat = lineVat(line);

        if (!vatMap.has(rate)) {
          vatMap.set(rate, { rate, base: 0, vat: 0 });
        }

        const entry = vatMap.get(rate);
        entry.base += base;
        entry.vat += vat;
      });
    });

  return Array.from(vatMap.values()).sort((a, b) => b.rate - a.rate);
}
```

**Added to src/reports.js:**

`lateFee(invoice, asOf)` calculates late fees at 0.04% of the amount due for each day overdue:
- Returns 0 if invoice isn't overdue (dueDate >= asOf) or has no dueDate
- Uses `balanceDue()` to get the unpaid amount (handles partially paid invoices)
- Calculates days overdue via `daysBetween(dueDate, asOf)`
- Fee = balanceDue × 0.0004 × daysOverdue, rounded to cents

**Added 9 comprehensive tests** covering:
- Returns 0 when not overdue
- Returns 0 on the due date
- Correct formula calculation (0.04% per day)
- Partially paid invoices use remaining balance
- Fully paid invoices have 0 fee
- Fee increases with more days overdue
- Works with both NET14 and NET30 terms
- Rounds to integer cents
- Handles missing dueDate gracefully
